To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the SIENAX segmentation algorithm without priors underestimates GM volume and overestimates WM volume, 2) the SIENX algorithm with priors agrees closely with SPM5 segmentation, 3) SPM5 and the SIENAX algorithm with priors both show the expected age-related changes in GM and WM volumes.
SIENAX, when using priors, provides close agreement with the SPM5 method for deriving volumes of cerebral grey and white matter.
the use of prior probability information improves the agreement between SIENAX and SPM5, but without prior probabilities the two methods are not in close agreement.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel, noninvasive, and cost-effective method for the diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease.
the validation of the two most commonly used automated brain segmentation tools.
the development of an accurate method to measure the volumes of grey and/or white matter in the brains of normal and diseased subjects.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of priors in SIENAX results in accurate and reproducible volumetric estimates, comparable to SPM5.
SPM5 and FSL-SIENAX provide similar estimates of grey and white volumes in the normal brain, but SIENAX needs priors for accurate estimates.
SPM5 and SPM8 are the best tools for brain segmentation, but only if priors are applied.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SPM5 and SPM5 with priors (SIENAX) provide accurate and reliable volumetric estimates of grey and white matters.
SIENAX with priors is a good alternative to SPM5.
SIENAX with priors and SPM are both excellent tools for automated brain volume estimation, with SIENAX being faster and more accurate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SIENAX without priors should be used with care.
it is critical to validate any automated segmentation tool against a gold standard, and to use the gold standard to define the priors required to obtain reliable estimates.
SIENAX without priors is not suitable for volumetric studies, and that SPM and SIENAX with priors can be used interchangeably for this purpose.
